text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Parliament did rejected a vote of no-confidence in Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs.

- The U.N. rejected consideration of a Russian motion of censure against Latvia and Estonia for alleged human rights violations against their local Russian minorities. The U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights, Jose Lasso, said there was no violation of human rights but there were problems with issuing identity documents to non-citizens, most of whom are Russians.
- Parliament adopted amendments to a law on rents which partly abolishes government-set restrictions on the rents in private and state-owned houses and flats.
- Former UNICEF national committee director and professor Anita Ushacka has been elected to the post of judge in the constitutional court.
- Sweden imposed a ban on the trips of the ferry Russ between Riga and Stockholm, which have only just resumed, as it does not meet Swedish safety requirements.
- Parliament established a commission to investigate the activities of the national radio and TV council.

- Latvian foreign policy experts doubt whether renouncing the 1920 peace treaty will help normalise Latvia's relations with Russia. They believe that before concluding the final agreement on the border with Russia, Latvia should improve relations with its eastern neighbour.
- On November 28, Latvia's internal debt amounted to 180.97 million lats, about five million lats more than a week before. The budget deficit was 21.6 million lats.

- The head of the Uzbek delegation which visited Latvia on November 26 said his country sees Latvia as a promising partner, especially in the field of exporting Uzbek natural resources through Latvian ports.
- The Latvian Privatisation Agency approved the rules of privatisation of RAF, Latvia's mini-van manufacturer.
